### New Songs of Praise
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/new-songs-of-praise-one-year-devotions-for-men-april-2.html
Passage: Psalm 33:1, 3
Points:
- "Worship wars" over musical styles needlessly divide believers across generational lines.
- Scripture teaches that music has an essential role in worship and must be directed to the Lord.
- The command to sing "new songs" shows there is a biblical place for contemporary music.
- Leading musical worship requires skill, preparation, and spiritual diligence.
- Every form of musical worship must remain firmly anchored in God's unchanging truth.

### Wisdom from the Psalms 3/29
Author: Crosswalk.com
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/wisdom/wisdom-from-the-psalms-3-or-29-552234.html
Passage: Psalm 33:6
Points:
- The Lord formed the vast heavens and starry hosts simply by the breath of His mouth.
- The splendor of the cosmos shows that nothing in all creation is outside of God's sovereign control.
- God's breath gives life to every creature and sustains human existence each day.
- Contemplating the Creator's boundless power and personal care inspires awe, praise, and rejoicing.

### We Can Trust God and Everything He Does: Praying through Psalm 33:1-5
Author: Scotty Smith
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/scotty-smith/we-can-trust-god-and-everything-he-does-praying-through-psalm-331-5/
Passage: Psalm 33:1-5
Points:
- Believers can rejoice and praise God because Christ's righteousness robes and redeems them.
- Artistic gifts and musical skill are divine provisions given to deepen our enjoyment of God.
- Even when life is confusing and timelines disappoint, God's Word and character remain entirely trustworthy.
- God's unfailing love actively orchestrates our lives and will one day fill the whole earth with justice.

### Sunday Morning Is Not About Me: The Joy of Self-Forgetfulness
Author: Stephen Witmer
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/sunday-morning-is-not-about-me
Passage: Psalm 33:1-22
Points:
- Psalm 33 uniquely pairs an enthusiastic call to worship with a unified congregational response of faith.
- True worship develops when we focus less on ourselves and more on the majesty of God.
- The psalmist motivates praise by highlighting God as speaking with power, reigning over nations, observing mankind, and saving from death.
- Lasting contentment comes through self-forgetfulness rather than cultural self-obsession.
- In Christ, believers see the ultimate fulfillment of God's Word, sovereign plan, and saving love.
